item.title: Study Finds AI-generated Code Fails to Boost Productivity Due to Downstream Bottlenecks
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/jellyfish-ai-productivity/en/headerimage/claude-built-c-compiler-1792676797236.jpeg"/><p>A recent Harvard study of 718 firms, using the Jellyfish analytics platform, finds that although AI coding assistants and agents increase code volume, this does not translate into a corresponding increase in completed work, partly because AI-generated code increases the workload in later stages of development, particularly code review.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

item.title: Presentation: Actors for Agents: Patterns for Production AI
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/actors-for-production-ai-agents/en/mediumimage/medium-1792065780503.jpeg"/><p>Manju Rajashekhar explains how the actor model solves the complex runtime challenges of production AI agents. By treating agents as distributed systems, he discusses state ownership, message passing, write-through state, and supervision boundaries to manage failures, continuations, and mutable execution graphs, moving agentic workflows beyond fragile demos to resilient architecture.</p> <i>By Manju Rajashekhar</i>

item.title: Vercel Labs Open-Sources fx: A Zig Coding Agent Designed to Be Embedded
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/vercel-zig-fx-agent/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792649903570.jpg"/><p>Vercel Labs has released fx, an experimental open-source coding agent written in Zig. It runs as a CLI, a script component, or an embedded library, including a WebAssembly build. Early feedback questioned its model-agnostic claim and a name conflict with an existing tool. Vercel says the project is pre-1.0 and changing quickly.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Article: AI Changes the Data Interface, Not the Query Engine
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/ai-changes-data-interface/en/headerimage/header-1792487239242.jpg"/><p>This article presents a disaster-recovery analytics workflow in which an AI agent generates constrained SQL or Python, DuckDB computes reproducible facts from Parquet, and the agent interprets the results. It explains the determinism split, replayable analysis, and four signals for deciding when an embedded engine is sufficient or a managed lakehouse is justified.</p> <i>By Peihao Yuan</i>

item.title: Harbor Adds Docker Sandboxes to Run Reproducible AI Agent Evals in Isolated MicroVMs
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/ai-agents-harbor-docker/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792589629439.jpg"/><p>Docker announced that Harbor, the open-source agent evaluation framework, now works with Docker Sandboxes. This change allows each evaluation task to run in its own microVM. So, instead of sharing a container, tasks are isolated for better performance</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

item.title: Developer Behind the AI-Built Adobe Clones Says They Are “Not Anywhere Close to Ready
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>A developer used Claude Opus 5.5 to build open-source replacements for seven Adobe applications, promoted them across Reddit with a projection of roughly 100% parity within a month, then told Hacker News the project was not anywhere close to ready. Its own roadmap puts it at 45% ready for real work and 2,300 to 4,100 agent-hours from full parity.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/emudhra-ca-compromise/en/headerimage/weak-link-1792602361259.jpeg"/><p>Private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates have been compromised, allowing attackers to forge certificates for any site. The keys were revealed due to low entropy, not through a known breach. Browsers blocked them using revocation lists, but other software had to remove the emSign ECC G3 root. Unpatched systems remain exposed to forged certificates, including client auth and mTLS.</p> <i>By Chris Swan</i>

item.title: Netflix Bridges AWS IAM and Internal Identity with Workload Attestation
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Netflix has developed a workload attestation mechanism for Apache Spark jobs running on Amazon EMR. The design combines AWS IAM identity with signed claims from Netflix’s control plane before issuing short-lived internal X.509 certificates, allowing managed compute workloads to authenticate to internal services without directly injecting credentials.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

item.title: Article Series: Agentic AI Architecture
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/agentic-ai-architecture-article-series/en/headerimage/agentic-ai-architecture-article-series-header-image-1792490151960.jpg"/><p>In this article series, we try to establish agentic AI architecture as a new type of software architecture that will likely dominate the industry for years to come. The articles, written by industry experts, cover various elements and aspects of agentic AI architecture. We aim to present the latest trends and developments shaping the new type of architecture as it enters the mainstream.</p> <i>By Rafał Gancarz</i>

item.title: Presentation: AI is an Amplifier: Scale High Performance, Not Dysfunction
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/dora-ai-adoption-engineering-performance/en/mediumimage/medium-1791447741420.jpg"/><p>Nathen Harvey shares insights from DORA research on AI adoption in software delivery. He explains why AI acts as an amplifier, how the DORA AI Capabilities Model drives outcomes, and why engineering leaders must evolve beyond bottlenecks like code reviews to achieve sustainable productivity, reduce delivery instability, and empower developers without burning out their teams.</p> <i>By Nathen Harvey</i>

item.title: Google SynthID Detector Simplifies Watermark Detection and Expands Support to Other AI Providers
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/synthid-watermarking-detector/en/headerimage/cyberark-model-security-1792576150415.jpeg"/><p>Google DeepMind announced the global availability of SynthID Detector, a tool designed to help identify AI-generated content, including media created using AI tools from SynthID partners such as OpenAI, NVIDIA, and Kakao, with Apple support expected soon.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

item.title: Article: Distributed Spring Batch Without a Message Broker
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/spring-batch-without-broker/en/headerimage/Distributed-Spring-Batch-Without-a-Message-Broker-header-1792419294298.jpg"/><p>Distributed Spring Batch partitioning already needs a shared, persistent job repository. This article makes that database the whole coordination plane and drops the message broker, sizing work to the live node count, a per-job master with no standing coordinator, compare-and-set claiming that prevents double-execution, two-phase heartbeat failover, and where a broker is still the right choice.</p> <i>By Janardhan Reddy Chejarla</i>

item.title: Cilium 1.20 Expands Gateway API and Opens eBPF Datapath for Kubernetes
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cilium-120-kubernetes-networking/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792161419866.jpg"/><p>Cilium 1.20 has been released with broader Kubernetes Gateway API support, an extensible eBPF datapath and further work on sidecarless mutual TLS. The release also makes the newer netkit network device easier to introduce across Kubernetes fleets that run different Linux kernel versions.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

The release also makes the newer netkit network device easier to introduce across Kubernetes fleets that run different Linux kernel versions.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

item.title: Microsoft Previews dotnetup: Toolchain Manager for .NET SDKs and Runtimes
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Microsoft has released a public preview of dotnetup, a cross-platform toolchain manager that installs and updates .NET SDKs and runtimes in the user’s own directory without admin rights. It tracks channels such as latest, lts, preview, and daily, reads global.json, and removes unused installs. Commands may still change before general availability.</p> <i>By Almir Vuk</i>

item.title: TornadoVM 7 Enables GPU-Native Workloads from Java Applications
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>TornadoVM, an open-source heterogeneous programming framework for Java, has reached version 7.0. It automatically accelerates Java programs on multi-core CPUs and GPUs and provides a rich GPU programming ecosystem in Java that can be used with any mainstream JDK distribution e.g. Temurin, Red Hat OpenJDK, Coretto, Oracle, GraalVM or Zulu.</p> <i>By Ben Evans</i>

item.title: GitHub Actions Runner Controller 0.15.0 Targets Reliability at Scale
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/github-runner-controller-0-15/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791971221854.jpg"/><p>GitHub has released Actions Runner Controller (ARC) 0.15.0, introducing reliability, scalability, and observability improvements for organisations running self-hosted GitHub Actions runners on Kubernetes.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

item.title: Buildkite Adds Scoped Secrets and New Agentic CI Tools
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/buildkite-ci-secrets-agentic/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792160661689.jpg"/><p>Continuous integration provider Buildkite has introduced pipeline-scoped secrets and new Model Context Protocol tools for validating pipelines, diagnosing failed builds and repairing webhooks. The company has also added Linux arm64 support to its GitHub Actions compatibility layer and expanded OpenTelemetry data in Buildkite Agent v4.1.0.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

item.title: NestJS 12: ESM Packages, Standard Schema Validation and Native Observability
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/nestjs-12-observability/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792168374584.jpg"/><p>NestJS version 12 has been released, transitioning core packages to ESM and adding Standard Schema validation. It updates the CLI and introduces an observability SDK. Key changes include project generation choices between CJS and ESM, improved validation options, and lifecycle project hooks. Users will need Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+. Migration guides are available for upgrading.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: AWS Introduces Preview of Well-Architected Agent
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/aws-well-architected-agent/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791124477134.jpg"/><p>AWS recently announced the preview of the Well-Architected Agent, a service that analyzes environments against Well-Architected best practices and provides prioritized recommendations across cost, security, performance, and reliability. The AI agent can also suggest remediation steps and review infrastructure-as-code before deployment.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

item.title: AWS Will Run Its European Sovereign Cloud Without the Global Backbone for Several Hours
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/aws-sovereign-cloud-exercise/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791945895599.jpg"/><p>On October 24, AWS will operate its European Sovereign Cloud without a connection to the AWS Global Network backbone, with a team of EU residents and the region’s own hardware and software. AWS says neither of the two systems being severed is operation-critical, and practitioners are divided over whether the exercise answers the question customers are asking.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Zod Brings In-Process Schema Compilation and a 9x Cut in Memory Footprint
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/zod-schema-compliation/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792163115814.jpg"/><p>Zod is a TypeScript-focused schema validation library that recently released versions 4.5 and 4.6. Key updates include schema compilation for faster data parsing, significant memory usage reductions, and new validation features. The library supports efficient validation processes and remains popular in the JavaScript ecosystem, achieving millions of downloads weekly.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: AI in Production: Panellists Highlight Silent Failures, Harness Engineering, and Agent Governance
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/ai-systems-production/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792118181680.jpg"/><p>A recent InfoQ webinar examined operational challenges in deploying agentic systems. Key points included issues like semantic and embedding drift, which can lead to significant errors. Experts discussed the need for automated code reviews, continuous evaluation of models, and enhanced privacy measures. The session emphasised a strategic approach to deployment and security management.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>

item.title: Grafana Applies SLOs and Error Budgets to AI Agent Behaviour
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/grafana-slo-ai-agent/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791475262295.jpg"/><p>Grafana Labs is proposing a familiar reliability engineering approach for one of the less familiar problems in modern software: how to measure whether an AI agent is actually behaving well.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

item.title: Mini book: Evolutionary Architecture in Practice
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/minibooks/evolutionary-architecture/en/smallimage/thumb-1791282847807.jpg"/><p>Discover how to keep software evolvable as systems, technology, and teams shift. This edition explores agentic fitness functions for semantic drift, treating human comprehension as a core design metric, cross-cloud guardrails for regional autonomy, and aligning technical boundaries with Conway’s Law. Move beyond static diagrams to continuous feedback systems that keep change safe and intentional.</p> <i>By InfoQ</i>

item.title: Presentation: Exploding GPUs and the AI Infrastructure Challenge
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/ai-security-kubernetes-gpu-threats/en/mediumimage/andrew-martin-medium-1790846331295.jpeg"/><p>Andrew Martin discusses why AI security is fundamentally tied to Kubernetes security. He shares insights into the evolving AI threat landscape, covering non-deterministic agent behavior, GPU supply chain vulnerabilities, shared compute risks, and practical defense strategies - from prompt firewalling to agentic identity - to help secure cloud-native AI workloads in production environments.</p> <i>By Andrew Martin</i>

item.title: Chainguard Launches Secure Workspaces and Checks for AI Coding Agents
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/chainguard-workspaces-checks/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792079610138.jpg"/><p>Software supply chain security company Chainguard has announced two beta products for running and testing code written by developers and AI agents. Chainguard Workspaces provides remote development environments based on hardened microVMs, while Chainguard Checks moves continuous integration into the development loop. The company announced both products at its Assemble London event.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

item.title: Cloudflares Newly Acquired Vite+ Reaches 1.0 with GitLab CI Support, Hooks, and tsup Migration
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-viteplus-stable/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791892196672.jpg"/><p>VoidZero has launched Vite+ 1.0, the first stable version of its JavaScript toolchain. It features a command line tool for managing Node.js, package management, and frontend development from a single configuration file. Enhancements include CI integration for GitLab and Docker support. Future updates are planned, focusing on stability and diagnostics.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: React 19.3: Adds a browser() API, Giving Client-Only Rendering a First-Class Name
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/react-19-3-browser-api/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791791785119.jpg"/><p>React 19.3 was released on September 9, introducing several features including the react-dom browser() API. This API allows components to opt out of server-side rendering, addressing issues with components that rely on client-specific data. It provides a cleaner solution for managing hydration mismatches and supports conditional data fetching, enhancing flexibility for developers.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>
